boundary_rationale: The book's opening word is אֵיכָ֣ה (oshb:Lam.1.1, byte tier), the verse-initial cry that gives this stretch its aleph line and frames a third-person report of the ruined capital: “How the city sits solitary, that was full of people! She has become as a widow, who was great among the nations!” web:Lam.1.1. The same voice names the daughter-of-Zion formula at web:Lam.1.6 inside “All majesty has departed from the daughter of Zion.” web:Lam.1.6 (this verse also carries a ketiv/qere note per the inventory, not engaged by the present reading; the formula itself recurs seven further times book-wide, sweep: 8 verses book-wide), and keeps the same distance through the roads, gates and priests of web:Lam.1.4. The report closes on “She has no comforter.” web:Lam.1.9 immediately followed by the first-person plea “See, Yahweh, my affliction; for the enemy has magnified himself.” web:Lam.1.9, a brief intrusion of Zion's own voice inside an otherwise third-person span (a per-bytes deviation from a plain city_lament reading, disclosed rather than smoothed over). The same verse completes the contiguous refrain אֵ֥ין מְנַחֵ֖ם לָ֑הּ (oshb:Lam.1.9, byte tier; roughly "she is without a comforter"; sweep of the two-word refrain: 3 verses book-wide, skeleton tier), and refrains close units under the owner-ruled seam law: the boundary sits here rather than folding this verse forward with the interjection that follows it.

boundary_rationale: The second poem opens on its own aleph line: אֵיכָה֩ (oshb:Lam.2.1, byte tier), the same verse-initial cry that opened the opening poem (sweep: 3 verses book-wide for the verse-initial site), framing “How has the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger!” web:Lam.2.1, where the daughter-of-Zion formula בַּת צִיּ֔וֹן (oshb:Lam.2.1, byte tier) names the object of a third-person report of divine wrath running across the rest of this stretch. boundary_rationale: The stretch opens at the narrator's own body: “My eyes fail with tears.
